chapter1.learningOutcomes: By the End of This Chapter

chapter1Index.aprende23SonidosAlfabeto: Learn the 23 sounds of the Benga alphabet, including special vowels and unique consonants.
chapter1Index.domina9CombinacionesDiptongos: Master the 9 diphthong combinations that produce unique sounds in the Benga language.
chapter1Index.aprende13CombinacionesTriptongos: Learn the 13 triphthong combinations, especially common in verb conjugations.
chapter1Index.completaTuComprensionCon: Complete your understanding with 16 simple consonants and 5 nasal consonant combinations.
chapter1Index.bengaMantieneCorrespondenciaEstricta: Benga keeps a strict correspondence between spelling and pronunciation. Everything that is pronounced is written, and vice versa: everything that is written is pronounced clearly and distinctly.
chapter1Index.soloVocalesEU: Only the vowels á, é and ü are "long" (marked with an accent). The others are short. This distinction is crucial for understanding different meanings.
chapter1Index.combinacionesMbNdNg: The combinations Mb, Nd, Ng, Nj, Ny represent unique nasal sounds. Understanding how to articulate them is essential for correct pronunciation.
chapter1Index.letraFuncionaTantoComo: The letter Y works both as a vowel and as a consonant. Its behaviour is crucial for understanding syllable and stress patterns in Benga.
chapter1Index.escuchaConAtencionUsa: Listen Carefully: Use the audio files to get familiar with the sounds before trying to pronounce them.
chapter1Index.tomaNotasEscribePalabras: Take Notes: Write down the example words and their meanings to strengthen your memory.
chapter1Index.practicaPronunciacionIntentaReproducir: Practise Pronunciation: Try to reproduce the sounds you hear. Repeated practice is key.
chapter1Index.conectaPatronesBuscaSimilitudes: Connect Patterns: Look for similarities between sound combinations to build a mental map of the phonology.
chapter1Index.revisionEspaciadaVuelveRevisar: Spaced Review: Go back over earlier sections regularly to consolidate your learning.
chapter1Index.vezDominesFundamentosFoneticos: Once you master the phonetic foundations of Benga, Chapter 2 will introduce you to the noun classification system. You will learn about the seven noun classes that are fundamental to Benga grammar.
chapter1Index.listoParaIniciarTu: Ready to start learning Benga? Select a section above to begin.
chapter1Index.subtitle: Preliminary Lessons: Phonetics and Sounds of Benga
chapter1Index.introduction: Chapter 1 lays the foundation for understanding the Benga language. We'll start with the writing system and fundamental sounds, from the basic alphabet to complex combinations of vowels and consonants. This chapter is essential for reading, writing, and pronouncing Benga correctly.
chapter1Index.outcome1: Identify and correctly pronounce all 23 sounds of the Benga alphabet
chapter1Index.outcome2: Understand the distinction between long and short vowels
chapter1Index.outcome3: Master the pronunciation of diphthongs and triphthongs
chapter1Index.outcome5: Read and write Benga words with spelling accuracy

chapter2Index.clasificacionNominalSistemaSiete: Noun classification: the seven-class system of Benga
chapter2Index.juegoTarjetasSingularPlural: Card game: singular, plural and classes

nounsIntro.clasificacionNombresDependeModo: The classification of nouns depends on the way they form their plurals and take their corresponding adjuncts. This is, without doubt, the most interesting part of the Benga language. Nouns that form their plural in the same way are grouped into one class, taking the same or similar adjectives.
nounsIntro.nombresFormanSuPlural: Nouns that form their plural in the same way belong to the same class and take the same adjuncts.
nounsIntro.contrasteConLenguasRomances: In contrast to the Romance languages, the change in plural formation occurs at the beginning of the root, not in the ending.
nounsIntro.adjuntosAdjetivosPronombresPreposiciones: Adjuncts (adjectives, pronouns, prepositions...) must agree with the class of the noun, in both singular and plural. These are elements that are linked to the noun, surround it or are attached to it as
nounsIntro.datoHistoricoTreceDiferentes: Historical note: Plurals can be formed in thirteen different ways in Benga. However, to simplify learning, we reduce them to seven main classes, grouping under one class all the nouns that take the same adjuncts, even if they do not form the plural in exactly the same way.
nounsIntro.concordanciaEsFundamentalBenga: Agreement is fundamental in Benga. When a noun belongs to a class, all the adjectives that accompany it must take the form corresponding to that class:
nounsIntro.estoSeraDesarrolladoMas: This will be developed further in later chapters. It also affects other adjuncts such as pronouns and prepositions, among others.
nounsIntro.memorizaPatronesInicialesPrimer: Memorise the initial patterns: The first step is to identify the initial form of the singular noun. This will automatically tell you the class and, therefore, the pattern it must follow in the plural.
nounsIntro.agrupaPalabrasPorClase: Group words by class: Don't memorise words at random. Instead, create groups of words belonging to the same class so you can see the pattern clearly.
nounsIntro.practicaConcordanciaNoAprendas: Practise agreement: Don't learn only isolated words. Use each noun with an adjective to train your intuition for agreement.
nounsIntro.estasListoParaExplorar: You are ready to explore each noun class. Start with Class 1, which is the simplest and most accessible.

irregularNouns.excepcionesNoSiguenPatrones: Exceptions that do not follow the standard patterns
irregularNouns.aunqueSistemaSieteClases: Although the seven-class system is very regular, Benga contains a number of nouns that do not follow the expected patterns. Salvado y Cos groups them into two sections: nouns that lack a singular and nouns that lack a plural.
irregularNouns.hayCiertaPorcionNombres: There is a certain group of nouns that express a quantity of something (especially liquids), which are never used in the singular, but always in the plural, taking the adjuncts of the plural. Some were introduced in the
irregularNouns.otrosMuchosNombresHay: There are many other nouns that are used only in the singular, and which take the adjuncts corresponding to that singular number.
irregularNouns.nombresSinSingularSuelen: Nouns without a singular usually express mass or collective concepts (liquids, quantities, masses)
irregularNouns.aunqueNombreCarezcaPlural: Even if a noun lacks a grammatical plural, quantity is expressed by other syntactic means
irregularNouns.nombresIrregularesSonRelativamente: Irregular nouns are relatively few compared with the total nominal vocabulary
irregularNouns.esRecomendableMemorizarlosExplicitamente: It is advisable to memorise them explicitly because they do not follow patterns that can be inferred
irregularNouns.memorizaListaNombresCarecen: Memorise the list of nouns that lack a singular and a plural
irregularNouns.usalosFrasesConAdjetivos: Use them in sentences with adjectives to practise correct agreement
irregularNouns.prestaAtencionComoSe: Pay attention to how quantity and modification are expressed with these nouns
irregularNouns.creaListaPersonalOtros: Create a personal list of other irregular nouns you find in your studies

verbalNouns.nombresDerivanOtrasPalabras: Nouns derived from other words can be divided into three classes: abstract nouns derived from verbal imperatives, agent nouns derived from verbal imperatives, and nouns of manner derived from agent nouns or abstract nouns.
verbalNouns.estosSeFormanSegunda: These are formed from the second person singular of the imperative, by removing the last syllable and placing the letter i before the word.
verbalNouns.clasificacionEstosNombresPertenecen: In the classification, these nouns belong to
verbalNouns.estosSeFormanAsimismo: These are likewise formed from the second person singular of the imperative, by removing the last syllable, placing the letter u before the word, and ending in the letter i.
verbalNouns.formacionPluralUMe: in the formation of the plural. u->me
verbalNouns.estosSeReformanMudando: These are re-formed by changing the initial "u" of the agent nouns to an "i", and adding "di" to their ending. (It could also be understood as replacing the last letter of the abstract nouns with "idi"
verbalNouns.dosPrimerasClasesNacen: The first two classes come from the second person singular of the imperative, without its last syllable
verbalNouns.claseSegundaEsaVocal: In the second class this vowel is dropped or changed, which gives the forms ulongi, ulangi, ukali
verbalNouns.claseTerceraParteNombre: The third class starts from the action noun: it changes its initial u to i and adds di at the end
verbalNouns.longakaUlongiEIlongidi: Longaka, ulongi and ilongidi show how a single verb root produces the three types
verbalNouns.tresDerivacionesAplicandoCada: The three derivations: applying each rule to the same verb root gives the three types of nouns. This is the case with the root "long" of Longaka, «build!»:
verbalNouns.memorizaTresReglasFormacion: Memorise the three formation rules and the starting form each one begins from
verbalNouns.tomaImperativoNuevoDeduce: Take a new imperative and work out its abstract noun and its action noun
verbalNouns.parteNombreAccionConstruye: Start from an action noun and build its noun of manner with the ending -di
verbalNouns.compruebaTablaResumenClase: Check in the summary table which noun class each form belongs to

practice.juegaConSingularPlural: Play with the singular, the plural and the noun classes
practice.cadaTarjetaMuestraSingular: Each card shows the singular with its audio. The translation stays hidden until you ask for it.
practice.pulsaIconoGiroPara: Press the flip icon (↺) to see the class and the conversion summary (for example i- → ma-).
practice.pulsaloNuevoParaRevelar: Press it again to reveal the plural with its audio.
practice.pulsaloUltimaVezPara: Press it one last time to go back to the singular. When you activate a card, the others return to their initial state.
practice.barajaNavegaPorPaginas: Shuffle and browse by pages (~10 cards on desktop, 2 on mobile).

regularAdjectives.adjetivosVariablesTomanSu: Variable adjectives take the form corresponding to singular and plural, agreeing in classification with the nouns they qualify. Each adjective varies according to the class of the noun it modifies. Each adjective of this type could have up to 7 different forms, depending on the noun class of the noun it refers to. For this reason, whenever we refer to a translation we will use one of these forms to simplify the explanation, but it is important to remember that every adjective of this type can vary according to the noun class of the noun. The declension rules are general, but there may be some exceptions to make pronunciation easier.
regularAdjectives.veamosComoSeDeclina: Let's see how the adjective is declined
regularAdjectives.buenoParaConcordarCon: (good) to agree with a noun of each class. The syllable
regularAdjectives.notaConPocasExcepciones: Note: With few exceptions, all adjectives vary in agreement with the noun of their respective class. The adjective 'būamu' (good) takes all these forms to agree with nouns of each class. Press the audio icon to listen to each noun and adjective combination.
regularAdjectives.buenoSeFlexionaAsi: (good) is inflected like this according to the class of the noun:

chapter3Index.adjetivosVariablesInvariablesComparativo: Variable and invariable adjectives, comparatives and numerals
chapter3Index.aprenderasEsteCapitulo: What will you learn in this chapter?
chapter3Index.singularPluralConSustantivo: (singular or plural) with the noun they modify. The
chapter3Index.condicionanPorTantoTodas: therefore determine all the words that accompany the noun (adjunct).
chapter3Index.partenFormaBaseSe: They start from a base form that is inflected to adapt to the seven classes of nouns.
chapter3Index.conservanFormaUnicaCualquier: They keep a single form in any context, without varying with the noun class.
chapter3Index.bengaCareceGradosFormales: Benga lacks formal degrees of comparison and resorts to circumlocutions or expressive turns of phrase.
chapter3Index.cincoPrimerosNumerosConcuerdan: The first five numbers agree like variable adjectives; ordinals use the declined preposition "de" plus the cardinal number.
chapter3Index.dominarEstasVariacionesE: Mastering these variations and inflections is fundamental to the structure and agreement of the Benga language.

invariableAdjectives.formasFijasNoCambian: Fixed forms that do not change
invariableAdjectives.adjetivosInvariablesNoVarian: Invariable adjectives do not vary and are used in the same way alongside the nouns they qualify, undergoing no change in their single, simple form. These adjectives have no number, gender or classification.
invariableAdjectives.escuchaCadaEjemploPulsando: Listen to each example by pressing the audio icon: the Benga language is mainly oral.
invariableAdjectives.siSegunClaseSustantivo: Yes, according to the noun's class
invariableAdjectives.sinDistincionComoTodos: No distinction (like all words in Benga)

comparatives.expresionComparacionGradoBenga: Expressing comparison and degree in Benga
comparatives.adjetivosBengaCarecenGrados: Adjectives in Benga lack the traditional degrees of comparison. However, objects are compared using a variety of means: circumlocution, particular intonation, understood emphasis, and especially the words
comparatives.seUtilizanParaComparar: Used to compare two or more objects, mainly with the words
comparatives.seUtilizanParaExpresar: Used to express the highest degree of a quality among several objects.
comparatives.hayFormaMasSencilla: There is a simpler form, better suited to Spanish: use
comparatives.sentidoMasEstaForma: in the sense of “more”. This form suits mainly those who have learned English, French, etc.
comparatives.porNoHayGrados: Why are there no traditional degrees of comparison?
comparatives.lenguaBengaComparativosSuperlativos: In the Benga language, comparatives and superlatives work through strategies that are more contextual than formal. The use of intonation, emphasis and circumlocution is essential for effective communication. The Benga people use a peculiar intonation and understood emphasis to indicate extremes of quality and quantity.
comparatives.estoDemuestraCaracteristicaImportante: This shows an important feature of the language: the importance of the “living voice” in conveying meaning, where prosodic elements are crucial to full understanding.

numerals.modoContarBengasEs: The Benga way of counting is strictly decimal. On reaching ten, reduplication takes place: ten and one, ten and two, etc.; two tens, three tens, etc., up to a hundred.
numerals.cincoPrimerosNumerales1: The first five numerals (1-5) are variable and change according to the noun's class.
numerals.ordinalesPropiamenteDichosNo: The Benga people do not know ordinals as such; however, there is a general way of expressing them. This method consists of prefixing the cardinal number in the possessive case.
numerals.distributivosSeFormanRepitiendo: Distributives are formed by repeating the cardinals.
numerals.mostrarDedosLevantadosEsperar: Show the raised fingers and wait for the listeners to say the number aloud. This method is very effective for representing hundreds, tens and units without ambiguity.
numerals.repetirPalabraDiezQuince: Repeat a word ten, fifteen or twenty times in great haste to indicate an extraordinary number, quality or quantity. It is typical of storytelling, especially among women.

home.bengaPerteneceFamiliaLenguas: Benga belongs to the Ndowe family of languages, spoken in Equatorial Guinea and adjacent regions. It is a language rich in grammatical nuances and unique sounds.
home.habladaPrincipalmenteIslaCorisco: Spoken mainly on the island of Corisco, the villages of its bay and adjacent islands in Equatorial Guinea. This region has a rich cultural and linguistic tradition.
home.bengaRepresentaParteImportante: Benga represents an important part of African linguistic heritage. Its preservation is essential to maintain cultural diversity and ancestral knowledge.
home.estePortalEstaBasado: This portal is based on the seminal work of Francisco Salvadó y Cos, published in 1891:
home.coleccionApuntesPreliminaresSobre: "Colección de apuntes preliminares sobre la lengua Benga, o sea introducción a una gramática de este idioma que se habla en la isla de Corisco, pueblos de su bahía e islas adyacentes"
home.obraOriginalPublicadaMadrid: The original work, published in Madrid by the Imprenta de A. Pérez Dubrull, represents the first systematic effort to document this language. Today we present it in an interactive digital format so that students of African languages, researchers and Benga speakers can access and learn from this valuable historical documentation.

home.sistemaClasificacionNombresSustantivos: Classification system of names and nouns in Benga.
home.aprendePronunciacionCorrectaCon: Learn the correct pronunciation with audio examples for each word.
home.accesoIntegradoLivingDictionary: Integrated access to the Living Dictionary to explore words in context.
home.aprendeCualquierDispositivoEscritorio: Learn on any device: desktop, tablet or mobile.
home.disponibleEspanolConSoporte: Available in Spanish, English and French.
home.basadoGramaticaHistoricaRigurosa: Based on the rigorous historical grammar of Salvadó y Cos.

about.retratoFranciscoSalvadoCos: Portrait of Francisco Salvadó y Cos
about.estaObraRepresentaPrimer: This work represents the first systematic effort to document the Benga language. In it, Salvadó y Cos presents a thorough introduction to Benga grammar, including:
about.alfabetoSonidosExplicacionDetallada: Alphabet and sounds: A detailed explanation of the writing and pronunciation system
about.vocalesDiptongosAnalisisFonetico: Vowels and diphthongs: Phonetic analysis of all vowel sounds
about.consonantesDescripcionConsonantesSimples: Consonants: Description of simple and combined consonants
about.nombresSustantivosSistemaClasificacion: Names and nouns: Noun classification system with seven classes
about.adjetivosAdjetivosVariablesE: Adjectives: Variable and invariable adjectives and their uses
about.ejemplosPracticosCientosPalabras: Practical examples: Hundreds of words and expressions in context
about.sigloXixEstudioLenguas: In the 19th century, the study of African languages was part of the European colonial enterprise. However, the work of Salvadó y Cos stands out for its scientific rigour and its respect for the language studied, gathering materials that would otherwise have been lost.
about.comoPrimerasDescripcionesSistematicas: As one of the first systematic descriptions of Benga, this grammar preserves invaluable information about the language that would otherwise be lost. For modern scholars of Benga and related languages, it is a primary source of critical importance.
about.comoMisioneroSalvadoCos: As a missionary, Salvadó y Cos spent years living among native Benga speakers. This closeness allowed him to gather authentic linguistic data directly from the speech community, rather than working with limited or second-hand informants.
about.obraSalvadoCosSigue: The work of Salvadó y Cos remains a reference in studies of Ndowe languages. His contribution to the documentation of Benga is recognised by modern African linguists and forms part of the collective intellectual heritage of the academic community.
about.estePortalDigitalRepresenta: This digital portal is an effort to make the valuable work of Salvadó y Cos accessible to new audiences. By transforming the 1891 grammar into an interactive format, we aim to:
about.preservarConocimientoLinguisticoHistoric: ✓ Preserve historical linguistic knowledge for future generations
about.facilitarAccesoEstudiantesLenguas: ✓ Make access easier for students of African languages around the world
about.apoyarHablantesNativosBenga: ✓ Support native Benga speakers in revitalising their language
about.contribuirDocumentacionLenguasPeligro: ✓ Contribute to the documentation of endangered languages
about.demostrarValorFuentesHistoricas: ✓ Demonstrate the value of historical sources for contemporary research
about.paraComplementarTuAprendizaje: To complement your learning on the portal, you can download the original grammar by Salvadó y Cos in PDF format:
about.bengaPerteneceFamiliaLenguas: Benga belongs to the Ndowe family of languages, which also includes Bubi (on Bioko) and other related languages spoken in the Gulf of Guinea region.
about.livingDictionaryEsRecurso: The Living Dictionary is a community resource that documents endangered languages. Browse the Benga words collected by the community of speakers.
about.silInstitucionLinguisticaVerano: SIL (Summer Institute of Linguistics) works on the documentation and preservation of minority languages worldwide, including Benga.
about.informacionSobreGeografiaCultura: Information about the geography, culture and languages of Equatorial Guinea, where Benga is spoken.

resources.obraCompleta1891Formato: The complete 1891 work in PDF format. This is the original document that forms the basis of this whole portal.

resources.institucionLinguisticaVeranoTrabaja: The Summer Institute of Linguistics works on the documentation of minority languages. Its resources include information on Ndowe languages and language documentation techniques.
resources.articuloInformativoSobreFamilia: Informative article on the Ndowe language family, including Benga. Provides geographic, historical and cultural context.

resources.informacionSobreIslaCorisco: Information about the island of Corisco and the surrounding area where Benga is spoken.
resources.informacionSobrePuebloNdowe: Information about the Ndowe people, their traditions and their cultural importance in the Gulf of Guinea region.
resources.contextoHistoricoAyudaEntender: Historical context that helps to understand the period in which Salvadó y Cos wrote his grammar.
resources.estudiosRecientesSobreDocumentacion: Recent studies on language documentation, language preservation and revitalisation.
resources.familiarizateConSonidosBasicos: Get familiar with the basic sounds and the Benga writing system before moving on to more complex structures.
resources.usaArchivosAudioDisponibles: Use the audio files available on the portal. Correct pronunciation is crucial in Benga.
resources.identificaPalabrasSeParecen: Identify words that resemble terms in other Ndowe languages or related Bantu languages.
resources.sistemaSieteClasesNominales: The system of seven noun classes is fundamental to Benga grammar. Take the time to learn them well.
resources.portalProporcionaCientosEjemplos: The portal provides hundreds of examples. Use them to see how the rules work in real context.
resources.siEsPosibleConecta: If possible, connect with native Benga speakers or communities of researchers interested in the language.

resources.livingDictionaryContribuyeCon: Living Dictionary: Contribute pronunciations and uses of Benga words
resources.silCommunitiesParticipaIniciativas: SIL Communities: Take part in language documentation and preservation initiatives
resources.comunidadNdoweBuscaGrupos: Ndowe Community: Look for Ndowe cultural and educational groups online or locally
resources.universidadesAlgunosProgramasLinguistica: Universities: Some African linguistics programmes may offer you specialised learning opportunities
resources.tienesRecursosAgregarCorrecciones: Do you have resources to add? Corrections or suggestions? We would love to hear from you.
